title: Topic 6.2: Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour

pages.lesson:
LESSON: HUMAN SEXUALITY: RESPONSIBLE SEXUAL BEHAVIOUR

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Christian Living Today
Topic 6.2: Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you live responsibly as a youth?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse
2. discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour
3. respect their bodies by living a morally upright life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HUMAN SEXUALITY: RESPONSIBLE SEXUAL BEHAVIOUR
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: HUMAN SEXUALITY: RESPONSIBLE SEXUAL BEHAVIOUR
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse

What this means
In this part you learn to identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Respect their bodies by living a morally upright life

What this means
In this part you learn to respect their bodies by living a morally upright life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respect their bodies by living a morally upright life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respect their bodies by living a morally upright life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Show how “Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour in your own words. (skill: discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: respect their bodies by living a morally upright life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse.
3. Practise this skill: discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour.
4. Practise this skill: respect their bodies by living a morally upright life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you live responsibly as a youth?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Human Sexuality: Responsible Sexual Behaviour means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify forms of sexual abuse and how to avoid or overcome abuse.
5. Be able to: discuss values and life skills needed to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
